node.name: next-env.d.ts
node.rich_text:
## What is `next-env.d.ts`?
It's a tiny **auto-generated TypeScript file** created by Next.js. You never write or edit it — Next.js manages it automatically.
---
### What it does:
```ts /// <reference types="next" /> /// <reference types="next/image-types/global" /> ```
These two lines tell TypeScript: - **"Load all Next.js type definitions"** — so TypeScript knows about `NextPage`, `GetServerSideProps`, `Metadata`, etc. - **"Load Next.js image types"** — so TypeScript understands `<Image>` component props
```ts import "./.next/dev/types/routes.d.ts"; ``` This loads **auto-generated route types** — so TypeScript knows all valid URL paths in your app.
---
### Simple analogy:
``` next-env.d.ts = a dictionary that tells TypeScript "here are all the Next.js words you're allowed to use" ```
---
### Key facts:
| Fact | Detail | |---|---| | **Auto-generated?** | Yes — by Next.js on every `npm run dev` | | **Edit it?** | Never — the file even says `// NOTE: This file should not be edited` | | **In `.gitignore`?** | Yes — never committed to GitHub | | **Without it?** | TypeScript would show errors on all Next.js features |
---
### Summary:
``` next-env.d.ts = auto-generated TypeScript glue file makes Next.js features work with TypeScript never touch it — Next.js owns it ```
It's one of the most boring but important files in a Next.js project — it just silently makes everything work.
